# Changelog

This file covers the repository itself — the toolchain, the rules and the documentation.

**Each package has its own changelog**, generated by changesets, and that is where the changes
that matter to a consumer are recorded:

- [`@deniscuciuc/maib`](packages/maib/CHANGELOG.md)
- [`@deniscuciuc/webshare`](packages/webshare/CHANGELOG.md)
- [`@deniscuciuc/bnm`](packages/bnm/CHANGELOG.md)
- [`@deniscuciuc/bnr`](packages/bnr/CHANGELOG.md)

The format is [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the packages follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) independently of one another.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-09-22

First publish of all four packages to npm. Released before any changeset
existed, so the per-package changelogs start from the next version.

### Added

- First public release of the repository. Four vendor clients — `maib`, `webshare`, `bnm` and
  `bnr` — published to npm under the `@deniscuciuc` scope, MIT licensed.
- The toolchain lives in the repository as files (`tsconfig.base.json`, `vitest.preset.ts`,
  `scripts/repo-kit/`) rather than as dependencies, so a clone builds and tests with nothing
  but a public npm registry.

### Fixed

- The `api` rule missed `export type { … } from …`, so a publicly exported type could be
  removed without the snapshot that exists to catch exactly that ever noticing.
  `WebsharePlanUsage` was in that position and is now covered.
- The package template exported `nodePreset` uncalled, so a package copied from it would have
  loaded no setup files and had no network stub at all — the suite's one hard rule would
  silently not have applied to it. It also lacked `tsconfig.test.json`, leaving its tests
  type-checked by nothing.

### Known issues

- The 0.1.0 tarballs were published **without a provenance attestation**. The
  workflow set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` in the job environment, but the variable
  did not survive `changeset publish` spawning pnpm. Fixed by `provenance=true`
  in a committed `.npmrc`, and the publish workflow now queries the registry
  afterwards and warns if an attestation is missing. The already-published
  0.1.0 tarballs cannot be attested retroactively; 0.1.1 onwards will be.
